title: Second London Baptist Confession of Faith (1689)
summary: The standard confession of Particular (Reformed) Baptists. Modeled after the Westminster Confession of Faith and the Savoy Declaration, with distinctly Baptist articles on baptism, church, and magistracy.

chapters.title: Of the Holy Scriptures
chapters.summary: The sufficiency, authority, inspiration, and self-attesting nature of Scripture as the only rule of faith and obedience.

chapters.title: Of God and of the Holy Trinity
chapters.summary: One God in essence, three Persons in subsistence — the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit; eternal, simple, holy, sovereign.

chapters.title: Of God’s Decree
chapters.summary: God’s eternal, unchangeable, and free decree — the foundation of providence, election, and reprobation.

chapters.title: Of Creation
chapters.summary: The world was created out of nothing in six days for God’s glory; man was made in the image of God, male and female.

chapters.title: Of Divine Providence
chapters.summary: God upholds, directs, and governs all things by His most wise providence — extending to the fall, free actions of men, and even the sins of angels and men.

chapters.title: Of the Fall of Man, of Sin, and of the Punishment Thereof
chapters.summary: Adam’s sin imputed; original sin and total depravity; the just punishment of death, both temporal and eternal.

chapters.title: Of God’s Covenant
chapters.summary: The covenant of works in Adam, the covenant of grace revealed and consummated in Christ — a single covenant variously administered.

chapters.title: Of Christ the Mediator
chapters.summary: The eternal Son took on real human nature, suffered, died, rose, ascended, and now intercedes — Prophet, Priest, and King of His people.

chapters.title: Of Free Will
chapters.summary: Man’s natural liberty, lost in the fall; the freedom of the will in the four states of innocence, sin, grace, and glory.

chapters.title: Of Effectual Calling
chapters.summary: The Spirit’s gracious work in drawing the elect from sin to Christ — irresistible, monergistic, and free.

chapters.title: Of Justification
chapters.summary: Sinners are accounted righteous through the imputed righteousness of Christ, received by faith alone.

chapters.title: Of Adoption
chapters.summary: The justified are received into the family of God, granted the privileges and inheritance of sons.

chapters.title: Of Sanctification
chapters.summary: The progressive work of God’s grace by which the saved are conformed to Christ in heart and life.

chapters.title: Of Saving Faith
chapters.summary: The nature, exercises, and degrees of saving faith — the means by which the elect receive Christ.

chapters.title: Of Repentance Unto Life and Salvation
chapters.summary: An evangelical grace by which the sinner, sensible of his sin, turns to God in Christ.

chapters.title: Of Good Works
chapters.summary: Good works are the fruit, not the cause, of saving faith — done in obedience to God’s commands and through His enabling grace.

chapters.title: Of the Perseverance of the Saints
chapters.summary: Those whom God has accepted in Christ shall certainly persevere — kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation.

chapters.title: Of the Assurance of Grace and Salvation
chapters.summary: True believers may infallibly be assured of their salvation — though the assurance is not of the essence of faith.

chapters.title: Of the Law of God
chapters.summary: The threefold use of the moral law — distinguished from the ceremonial and judicial laws now abolished.

chapters.title: Of the Gospel and the Extent of Its Grace
chapters.summary: The promise of Christ from the first promise in Eden, increasing in clarity until His coming — freely offered to sinners.

chapters.title: Of Christian Liberty and Liberty of Conscience
chapters.summary: Christ has purchased liberty from sin, the curse of the law, and the bondage of human traditions in matters of faith.

chapters.title: Of Religious Worship and the Sabbath Day
chapters.summary: The regulative principle: God may only be worshiped as He has prescribed; the Lord’s Day as the Christian Sabbath.

chapters.title: Of Lawful Oaths and Vows
chapters.summary: Oaths and vows are lawful when used soberly and in matters of weight — taken in God’s name only.

chapters.title: Of the Civil Magistrate
chapters.summary: Civil government is ordained by God for the public good; Christians may lawfully serve, obey, and pray for the magistrate.

chapters.title: Of Marriage
chapters.summary: Marriage is to be between one man and one woman; intended for mutual help, the increase of mankind, and the prevention of uncleanness.

chapters.title: Of the Church
chapters.summary: The universal church, particular local churches, the offices of pastor and deacon, the duties of members, and the right of association.

chapters.title: Of the Communion of Saints
chapters.summary: All saints united to Christ in faith, love, and gifts — bound to communion with one another in worship and care.

chapters.title: Of Baptism and the Lord’s Supper
chapters.summary: The two ordinances Christ instituted in His church — baptism and the Lord’s Supper — and their proper subjects and administration.

chapters.title: Of Baptism
chapters.summary: The baptism of believers by immersion, signifying union with Christ in His death and resurrection.

chapters.title: Of the Lord’s Supper
chapters.summary: The sacred memorial of Christ’s death — a means of strengthening faith, comforting believers, and visibly distinguishing the church from the world.

chapters.title: Of the State of Man After Death and of the Resurrection of the Dead
chapters.summary: The intermediate state, the bodily resurrection of the just and the unjust, and the certainty of judgment.

chapters.title: Of the Last Judgment
chapters.summary: Christ shall judge the world in righteousness on the appointed day — believers received into glory, the wicked into eternal punishment.
